question.text: Board representation rights allow an AIF investor to:

answer.text: Replace the entire board of directors of the investee company
Nominate one or more directors to the board of the investee company
Directly manage the day-to-day operations of the investee company

explanation.text: The Logic: Board-seat / board-representation terms in the share-subscription agreement give the AIF the right to nominate one or more directors to the investee company's board. This supports monitoring of the investment and a defined board-representation approach, while nominee directorships must be managed under the AIF's conflict and disclosure policy. The Trap: Board representation does not equal management control — the AIF does not run day-to-day operations, replace the entire board, or hold a unilateral veto over every board decision. Note: Removed the fiduciary-duty-to-company language and the "nominees cannot solely act in the AIF's interest" caveat — that legal-duty framing goes beyond what the checked workbook states. The explanation is now anchored on workbook-supported nominee appointment, monitoring, board-representation approach, and conflict/disclosure policy. Keyed answer is unchanged.
